nodes.name: NiMoO₄·xH₂O precursor synthesis
nodes.procedure: Self-supported NiMoO₄·xH₂O precursor was grown in situ on conductive substrates (nickel or copper foam) through the first-step water bath reaction (see experimental details in the Methods). The XRD pattern indicates the successful synthesis of the NiMoO₄·×H₂O phase through the first-step water bath reaction.
nodes.source_text: self-supported NiMo-H₂ catalyst was grown in situ on conductive substrates (nickel or copper foam, Supplementary Fig. S3) through a two-step water bath reaction and hydrogen reduction procedure... The XRD pattern in Supplementary Fig. S4a indicates the successful synthesis of the NiMoO₄·×H₂O phase through the first-step water bath reaction.

nodes.name: NiMo-H₂ hydrogen reduction
nodes.procedure: After hydrogen reduction in the second step at 500°C, the NiMoO₄·×H₂O precursor transformed into Ni₀.₉₁Mo₀.₀₉ alloy nanoparticles (20-40 nm) on MoO₂ nanorod matrix, constituting the NiMo-H₂ catalyst. A series of NiMo-H₂ samples were synthesized by varying the hydrogen reduction temperature over the range from 300 to 600°C. The sample reduced at 500°C exhibited the highest catalytic activity.
nodes.source_text: After hydrogen reduction in the second step, the NiMoO₄·×H₂O precursor transformed into Ni₀.₉₁Mo₀.₀₉ and MoO₂ phases... a series of NiMo-H₂ samples were synthesized by varying the hydrogen reduction temperature over the range from 300 to 600°C. Among the synthesized NiMo-H₂ samples, the one reduced at 500°C...

nodes.description: HER performance in 1 M KOH freshwater
nodes.source_text: The HER polarization curves in Fig. 3a show that the optimal NiMo-·H2 catalyst requires low overpotentials of 33 and 100 mV to reach current densities of 10 and 100 mA cm−2 (geometrical area > 0.8 cm², scan rate: 1 mV s−1, 90% iR compensation), respectively... It also exhibits a smaller Tafel slope value (47.4 mV dec−1, Fig. 3b)

nodes.description: HER performance in 1 M KOH seawater under one sun irradiation
nodes.source_text: As shown by the HER polarization curves in Fig. 4a, the NiMo-·H2 catalyst requires overpotentials of 23 and 89 mV to reach the current densities of 10 and 100 mA cm−2, respectively, in 1 M KOH seawater under simulated one sun irradiation... It also exhibits a small Tafel slope of 63.5 mV dec−1 in the photothermal electrolyzer

nodes.description: HER stability at 500 mA/cm² in 6 M KOH seawater under one sun
nodes.source_text: As a result, the NiMo-·H2 catalyst can sustain continuous testing for 540 h at a constant current density of 500 mA cm−2 in 6 M KOH seawater electrolyte... this NiMo-·H2 catalyst suffers a fluctuation in potential of only 66 mV over 540 h of durability testing

nodes.description: Overall seawater electrolysis in photothermal AEM electrolyzer (6 M KOH seawater, area 2.25 cm²)
nodes.source_text: The NiMo-H2||NiFe LDH pair requires low voltages of approximately 1.40, 1.51, and 1.80 V to reach absolute currents of ~0.0225, 0.225, and 1.8 A (area: 2.25 cm²), respectively, in 6 M KOH seawater under one sun irradiation and can work at a constant current of 0.45 A for 192 h... the energy efficiency of this photothermal AEM electrolyzer was calculated to be ~76.8% under light irradiation

nodes.source_text: NiMo-H2||NiFe LDH pair... can work at a constant current of 0.45 A for 192 h... demonstrating good catalytic repeatability over 192 h of durability testing

nodes.characterization_summary: NiMo-H2 catalyst shows Ni0.91Mo0.09 alloy and MoO2 phases after hydrogen reduction of NiMoO4·xH2O precursor.
nodes.evidence_snippet: After hydrogen reduction in the second step, the NiMoO4·xH2O precursor transformed into Ni0.91Mo0.09 and MoO2 phases (Supplementary Fig. S4c), thereby constituting the NiMo-H2 catalyst.

nodes.characterization_summary: Raman peaks at 818, 889, and 938 cm⁻¹ attributed to Mo-O vibration are much weaker in NiMo-H2 than precursor; Ni-O-Mo peak at ~371 cm⁻¹ sharply reduced with no Ni-O peak.
nodes.evidence_snippet: As shown in Supplementary Fig. S4d, the intensity of the Raman peaks at 818, 889, and 938 cm⁻¹ in the spectrum for the NiMo-H2 catalyst... is much weaker than that for the NiMoO4·xH2O precursor.

nodes.characterization_summary: NiMo-H2 preserves macroscopic nanorod structure with nanoparticles (20-40 nm) formed on nanorod surfaces.
nodes.evidence_snippet: upon hydrogen reduction, the structure of these nanorods underwent different changes in NiMo-H2: the macroscopic nanorod structure was preserved... but nanoparticles with a size distribution between 20 and 40 nm were newly formed on the surfaces of these nanorods.

nodes.characterization_summary: TEM confirms nanoparticles (20-40 nm) on MoO2 nanorods in NiMo-H2 with hierarchical structure.
nodes.evidence_snippet: upon hydrogen reduction, the structure of these nanorods underwent different changes in NiMo-H2: the macroscopic nanorod structure was preserved... but nanoparticles with a size distribution between 20 and 40 nm were newly formed on the surfaces of these nanorods (Fig. 1c, d, Supplementary Fig. S7d–f, and Supplementary Fig. S8a–c).

nodes.characterization_summary: HRTEM shows lattice fringes of 0.206 nm corresponding to (111) plane of Ni0.91Mo0.09 alloy in nanoparticles and 0.240 nm corresponding to (202) plane of MoO2 in nanorods.
nodes.evidence_snippet: As shown in the HRTEM images in Fig. 1e–g... the interplanar spacings of the lattice fringes in the nanoparticles measured 0.206 nm, which corresponds to the (111) plane of the Ni0.91Mo0.09 alloy, whereas lattice stripes with an interplanar spacing of 0.240 nm were detected in the rods, which corresponds to the (202) plane of MoO2.

nodes.characterization_summary: SAED confirms coexistence of Ni0.91Mo0.09 (111, 200 facets) and MoO2 (031 facet) phases in NiMo-H2.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The coexistence of Ni0.91Mo0.09 and MoO2 phases in NiMo-H2 catalyst was also confirmed by the SAED and TEM EDS mapping results.

nodes.characterization_summary: EDS mapping shows Ni only in nanoparticles, Mo and O throughout nanorod; single nanoparticle TEM EDS confirms Ni/Mo ratio of 9/1.
nodes.evidence_snippet: TEM EDS mapping images in Fig. 1h show that elemental Ni can only be found in the nanoparticles, while elemental Mo and O were observed throughout the entire nanorod. Detailed TEM EDS spectral analysis on single nanoparticle confirms... the Ni/Mo ratio of 9/1.

nodes.characterization_summary: BET surface area of NiMo-H2 is 48.3 m² g⁻¹, 3.5 times higher than NiMoO4·xH2O precursor (13.7 m² g⁻¹).
nodes.evidence_snippet: As shown in Supplementary Fig. S9, the BET surface area of NiMo-H2 catalyst (48.3 m² g⁻¹) is around 3.5 times that of the NiMoO4·xH2O precursor (13.7 m² g⁻¹).

nodes.characterization_summary: Ni XPS shows Ni⁰ 2p peaks at 853.6 and 870.2 eV in NiMo-H2 (vs Ni²⁺ at 856.2, 873.8 eV in precursor); Mo XPS shows Mo⁴⁺ 3d peaks at 230 and 233.2 eV in NiMo-H2 (vs Mo⁶⁺ at 232.4, 235.6 eV); reduced O 1s Mo-O peak intensity.
nodes.evidence_snippet: In the high-resolution Ni XPS spectrum for the NiMoO4·xH2O precursor (Fig. 1i), two peaks assigned to Ni²⁺ 2p3/2 and Ni²⁺ 2p1/2... After hydrogen reduction, the peaks attributed to Ni²⁺ 2p disappear, and two new peaks located at 853.6 and 870.2 eV... emerge for NiMo-H2.

nodes.characterization_summary: Ni K-edge XANES shows metallic Ni nature in NiMo-H2 similar to Ni foil; EXAFS shows Ni-Ni CN=6.4, Ni-Mo CN=1.4.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Ni K-edge X-ray absorption near edge structure (XANES) spectra in NiMo-H2 present a similar absorption edge to that of the Ni foil reference... fitting data... shows the NiMo-H2 model has an average Ni-Ni coordination number (CN) of 6.4 and an average Ni-Mo CN of 1.4.

nodes.characterization_summary: Self-supported NiMo-H2 shows reflectance <3% over 250-1500 nm wavelength range.
nodes.evidence_snippet: the self-supported NiMo-H2 exhibits a low reflectance of less than 3% over the wavelength range from 250 to 1500 nm (Fig. 2a).
